title: Digital customer service: The coordination behind every good answer
summary: Learn what digital customer service is in B2B. Find examples of how teams use channels to deliver efficient, consistent communication.
body_markdown:
Learn what digital customer service is in B2B. Find examples of how teams use channels to deliver efficient, consistent communication.


Digital customer service is nothing new. Plenty of customers already use messaging tools and would take them over a phone tree any day.


And yet plenty of B2B teams still struggle with it. Front’s[Coordination Tax Report](https://research.front.com/) found that 64% of companies had at least one customer-facing coordination failure in the past three months. For large companies with complex operations, keeping a conversation connected as it moves between stakeholders is easier said than done.


This article covers what digital customer service is and how to deliver it well in[B2B customer operations](https://front.com/blog/customer-service-operations) . Find techniques to improve coordination and keep customer context visible while teams work on an issue together.


## Why B2B teams need reliable customer service strategies


As a B2B company grows, digital customer service gets operationally complex fast, with more customers, more requests, more stakeholders, and more internal teams.


Not every digital customer service platform can handle that. Front’s[Coordination Tax report](https://research.front.com/) found that most systems are built for a single customer asking a single rep a question, and that anything more complex can take weeks to resolve.


Here’s why B2B teams need digital customer service tools built for coordination.


### Customer conversations rarely stay within one team


Complex B2B issues usually pull in multiple departments. A rep can respond fast and communicate well, but if they hand the issue off without flagging who owns it next, it still stalls.


Consider a digital customer service example typical in B2B: A logistics customer complains about a delayed shipment. Support replies quickly and gathers the details, but can’t give an updated delivery time until dispatch and operations figure out the cause and schedule a new slot.


### Teams need customer context across channels


When a customer messages you on Slack, they expect you to connect it to the emails they sent earlier or the same problem they had last month. Every interaction should build on the last, whatever channel they use, whichever team they reach, so customers never have to repeat themselves or start from scratch.


Say a manufacturing customer raises a production issue with support. It’s urgent, so support escalates to operations and fulfillment. To fix it, those teams need to see exactly what the customer said on both live chat and email, plus the account history to check whether this has come up before.


## How to provide effective digital customer service


In B2B, quality service isn’t just the interaction, it’s what happens behind it. As customer work gets more complex, you have to keep conversations and context connected. Here’s how.


### Give every team the customer context they need


Find[customer service software](https://front.com/blog/customer-service-software) that carries context from the earlier conversations. When a customer starts on chat and follows up by email or Slack, it won’t throw anyone off.


### Maintain clear ownership


The right tools make sure everyone knows who’s on the hook after a handoff. When support passes a billing discrepancy to finance, the handoff should carry a named owner and a deadline. The goal is simple: Every team knows who owns each request and what happens next.


### Use smart automations


Use automated workflows to coordinate work across teams. When a manufacturing customer reports an order about to miss its delivery date, automation can tag it as urgent and route it to production and fulfillment for prioritization. Self-service tools take routine work off your team’s plate, too.


### Incorporate AI while retaining control


Use AI assistants and agents to resolve simple queries through self-service knowledge bases and chatbots. For more complex cases, let AI read the content of a message and route it, then lean on your team’s judgment to actually resolve it.


## How leading organizations improve digital customer service


You can add every digital customer communication channel with AI-powered tools and automation features, and still see nothing improve.


That’s because customer work is usually fragmented across teams and systems, with limited analytics. In Front’s[Coordination Tax report](https://research.front.com/) only 5% of B2B companies said they use a tool that gives them a complete picture of customer work, including handoffs, coordination time, and duplicate work.


The teams that get digital customer service right tend to do these four things.


### Connect customer conversations across teams and channels


As work moves from customer support to operations, customer success, and beyond, make sure everyone is using the same[communication platform](https://front.com/blog/customer-communication-platform) and seeing the same context. Pull messages from different stakeholders and channels into a single shared inbox or conversation thread, with relevant operational data right there.


[Echo Global Logistics](https://front.com/customer-stories/echo) moved from siloed systems to Front, a single collaborative platform. Teams now have access to all the relevant customer messages, plus real-time shipment data from their transportation management system, all in one place. Fifteen months in, they’d already saved 1,000 hours of work.


### Build clear ownership into customer workflows


To cut coordination time, set simple rules for who owns each request. Build workflows so when work is handed off, it lands with a new, clearly labeled owner, and[use automation](https://front.com/blog/customer-service-automation) to route issues by consistent rules instead of routing them by hand.


Travel management company[Gattinoni Business Travel](https://front.com/customer-stories/gattinoni-business-travel) uses Front’s automated rules and workflows to categorize and route 7,200 daily emails. Reps tag, prioritize, and assign each request, tracking ownership start to finish. The result: a 15% improvement in response times.


### Define where AI helps


Point AI at the routine tasks, and keep your team on the complex and sensitive ones. Front’s[State of Service Expectations](https://front.com/assets/resources/downloads/the-state-of-service-expectations.pdf) report found customers still value being able to reach a human, and tie it to high-quality service.


Learning and career platform[Podium Education](https://front.com/customer-stories/podium-education) strikes this balance by using an AI assistant for most queries while applying different levels of automation based on the sensitivity of the inquiry. With Front, the team automated more than 3,000 conversations and saved more than 100 hours.


### Track handoffs and ownership, not just response times


Look past the usual response and resolution times, and watch how work actually moves across teams at each handoff. Dig into the delays to surface the patterns creating bottlenecks.


Front’s[Coordination Tax report](https://research.front.com/) found that just one in seven companies spends more time solving problems than coordinating. Take the operational friction out and you win back that coordination time for actually resolving issues.


Logistics firm[sennder](https://front.com/customer-stories/sennder) used Front’s integrations with Salesforce, Asana, Slack, Aircall, and Looker to create a 360-degree view of customer data and communication. Teams see everything from those platforms inside Front, so nobody’s logging into five tools to find one answer.


## How Front helps organizations deliver digital customer service at scale


Strong digital customer service in B2B comes down to strong coordination. Front gives teams what they need to coordinate work across departments and scale customer operations without giving up service quality.


Healthcare staffing marketplace[Trusted Health](https://front.com/customer-stories/trusted-health) serves more than a million clinicians and runs on Front to keep service quick and effective. The team leans on shared inboxes and assignment workflows to collaborate on customer requests and hand off issues cleanly, while rules and automations route messages to the right person. The same tools work whatever industry your B2B company is in.

## FAQ


### Which metrics measure digital customer service performance?


Use[customer support metrics](https://front.com/blog/customer-service-analytics) like first response time and time to resolution to track operational efficiency. Indicators like customer satisfaction and Net Promoter Score measure the quality of the customer experience.


### What should you look for in digital customer service software?


Look for[omnichannel support](https://front.com/blog/omnichannel-customer-support) , AI-powered chatbots, automated workflows, self-service portals, knowledge bases, customer relationship management tool integration, and strong analytics dashboards.


### How can businesses transition to digital customer service?


Start by digging into customer needs and their preferred digital customer service channels. Then focus on improving cross-team collaboration, so you can coordinate responses effectively across multiple channels and touchpoints.
